answer: The heart is a muscle that pumps blood in two loops, to the lungs and around the body. Blood comes in through the top chambers and leaves through the bottom ones.
title: How the human heart works
layout: a large front view of the heart in the middle; the top chambers at the top, the big left ventricle on the right of the picture, the right ventricle on the left; the vessels rise from the top; names on both sides
intro: A heart is soft and alive, so I drew it flat instead of in 3D. Let's trace the blood through it.
summary: Blood enters the atria, the ventricles pump it out, and the great vessels carry it to the lungs and the body.

parts.label: Heart wall
parts.say: This is the outer wall of the heart. It is a strong muscle that keeps working all your life.

parts.label: Atria
parts.say: The two top chambers, the atria, receive blood coming back to the heart.

parts.label: Right ventricle
parts.say: The right ventricle pumps blood to the lungs to pick up oxygen.

parts.label: Left ventricle
parts.say: The left ventricle has the thickest wall and pumps blood to the whole body.

parts.label: Septum
parts.say: The septum is the wall that keeps the left and right sides apart.

parts.label: Great vessels
parts.say: The aorta carries oxygen rich blood out to the body. The pulmonary artery carries blood to the lungs.

parts.label: Blood flow
parts.say: Arrows show the path. Blood enters the right atrium, goes to the lungs, comes back to the left atrium, then leaves through the aorta.
